title: Add metric label incident_type to request error metrics (with cardinality guardrails)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Internal-only. Adds a low-cardinality incident_type label to selected request error metrics and sampled logs to enable incident reporting by taxonomy.
body:
Title: Add metric label incident_type to request error metrics (with cardinality guardrails)

Context
This PR is part of the Reliability Program work to make incident taxonomy measurable in our telemetry (ENG-4826). We already require incident_type during incident creation/closure in incident-bot; this change makes it possible to break down error spikes by taxonomy category in dashboards without relying on freeform tags.

What this changes
1) Metrics
- Adds a new Prometheus label: incident_type to the following metrics:
  - redwood_gateway_request_errors_total
  - redwood_router_request_errors_total
  - redwood_request_errors_total (service-aggregated rollup)
- We only add incident_type on error-path increments (HTTP 5xx and explicit error codes) to avoid expanding cardinality on the success-path.

2) Source of truth / mapping
- incident_type is derived from existing structured fields that already have bounded enums:
  - gateway.error_class
  - router.failure_reason
  - auth.denial_reason
- Introduces a small allowlisted mapping table (taxonomy v1 top-level types only; no subtype labels in metrics for v1).
  - Example mappings:
    - router.failure_reason=CAPACITY_SATURATION -> incident_type=capacity
    - router.failure_reason=FALLBACK_LOOP -> incident_type=routing
    - gateway.error_class=UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT -> incident_type=latency
    - auth.denial_reason=RBAC_POLICY_EVAL_ERROR -> incident_type=auth
- When a request error does not match the allowlist, we set incident_type=unknown (instead of emitting unbounded strings).

3) Cardinality guardrails
- incident_type is a fixed enum string set: [availability, latency, streaming, routing, capacity, control_plane, auth, telemetry, private_connectivity, security_alignment, unknown].
- We do NOT attach incident_subtype (per workshop guidance) and we do NOT attach any customer-/org-/model-specific identifiers.
- For high-volume logs, we add incident_type as a structured field only on sampled error logs (existing error sampler; default 1:50, configurable by service).
- Adds a CI-time guardrail test that fails if the mapping table contains values outside the known enum set or if label count increases on protected metrics.

Why now
- The dashboard spec requires at least one stable label we can aggregate on across services. Without this, incident dashboards end up relying on incident-bot metadata only (which does not help correlate to error budgets and burn rates in Prometheus).

How to test
- Unit tests:
  - taxonomy_mapping_test: verifies known reasons map to expected incident_type and unknown reasons map to unknown
  - metrics_label_guardrail_test: ensures incident_type label is only present on the allowed metrics and not added to high-cardinality per-route series
- Manual:
  - trigger a synthetic 5xx in dev and confirm series appear with incident_type=availability or unknown depending on error_class
  - verify sample error logs include "incident_type" when the sampler keeps the event

Rollout plan
- Safe-by-default: unknown is the fallback, and the label is only attached to three existing metrics.
- After merge: Observability will watch TSDB series count and top-label cardinality for 48 hours.
- If series count increases unexpectedly, we can disable the label via config flag metrics.enable_incident_type_label=false (added in this PR) and redeploy.

Related work
- Confluence: Incident taxonomy dashboards spec (eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/incident-taxonomy-dashboards-spec)
- PRs:
  - pr-28437 (router fallback_reason enums)
  - incident-bot pr-812 (required incident_type dropdown)

Screenshots / examples
- Example metric (router): redwood_router_request_errors_total{cluster="us-east-1",service="router",incident_type="capacity",code="503"} 12
- Example log field: {"level":"error","msg":"upstream timed out","error_class":"UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT","incident_type":"latency",...}

Checklist
- [x] No customer identifiers added
- [x] Bounded label value set (allowlist)
- [x] Sampling for logs
- [x] Tests + CI guardrail
- [x] Backward compatible (label addition only)

Review conversation (highlights)
- Allison Grant (Observability): "We can’t attach incident_subtype yet; it will explode cardinality once people start adding more subtypes. Also please make the mapping table an allowlist and ensure unknown is the default." 
  - Sergio Costa: "Agreed. Removed incident_subtype label entirely, added TaxonomyIncidentType enum + allowlist mapping, and set unknown as fallback. Added a guardrail test to prevent drift."
- Aisha Bello (SRE dashboards): "Can we ensure this label is not added to per-route metrics? Dashboard queries should use only the rollup + gateway/router error totals." 
  - Sergio Costa: "Yes—scoped to *_request_errors_total only. Per-route and per-model metrics unchanged."
- Rafael Mendes (SRE): "We need a kill switch; if this increases series count we should be able to disable quickly." 
  - Sergio Costa: "Added metrics.enable_incident_type_label config flag default true; can be toggled at runtime where supported, otherwise via redeploy."
- Mei Lin (Data): "Please document which underlying reasons map to which incident_type; we’ll use it when backfilling last 90 days." 
  - Sergio Costa: "Added docs block in code comments + in /docs/ops/telemetry/incident_taxonomy_metrics.md with the current mapping table and rationale."

CI
- Build: pass
- Unit tests: pass
- Lint: pass
- Observability schema checks: pass

Outcome
Merged via squash into main. Follow-up: Observability-pack will update dashboard queries to prefer incident_type label where available (tracked separately).
commits: obs: add TaxonomyIncidentType enum and allowlisted mapping
metrics: attach incident_type label to gateway/router request error counters
logs: add incident_type to sampled error logs
docs: document mapping and dashboard query guidance
